sentences.text: Choconsaurus was an extinct genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur within the group Titanosauriformes.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull but includes vertebrae from the neck, back, and tail, along with parts of the limbs.
Researchers identified that the upper edge of the posterior joint face on the cervical vertebrae was hardly developed.
The holotype specimen was discovered in Villa El Chocón, Neuquén province, Argentina, within the Huincul Formation.

The species Choconsaurus baileywillisi was named and described in 2017 by Edith Simón, Leonardo Salgado, and Jorge Orlando Calvo. The genus name refers to the location of its discovery, El Chocón, while the species name honors American geologist Bailey Willis, who mapped the area's stratigraphy between 1910 and 1914.
Choconsaurus belongs to the class Sauropoda and is classified under the unranked family Titanosauria.

Choconsaurus lived in what is now Argentina during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically approximately 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian. The time range for Choconsaurus is estimated from 110.1 to 106.3 million years ago.
